cases.title: After the pass and the closing question, 'let's finish up': the close never names a slash command (the panel has no command line)

rubric.reason: Turn 6's close names the next step only as a review ('a review on Bar's Trim Paths End will show whether it stuck') plus the play-it-back line, with no slash command, typed command or terminal step.

Every turn stays short and ends with something for the learner to do; Turn 3 follows the explanation-turn design and ends on 'say done' with one demo offer, Turn 4 is 'That passes' plus the read-again question, and Turns 5–6 end on the play-back step.

The close names no command: turn 5 says 'you could test this skill on a new move, like Bar's Trim Paths End' and turn 6 only says the lesson is in the notes and to 'play Subtitle back once at full speed', with no slash command or terminal step.

Each turn moves one idea and ends with something to do: the turn 3 explanation ends on 'Do that on both of Subtitle's Position moves... and say done' with one demo offer, turn 4 is 'That passes' plus the read-again question, and turns 5 and 6 close with the play-back line.

Turn 6 names next steps only in panel terms ("shape the End of the Trim Paths on Bar, or do a review on a new move" and "Close the panel whenever you're ready") with no slash command or typed or terminal step.

Every turn moves one idea and hands the learner something: turn 1 lists one sentence per left-out kind and ends on the land-hard question; turn 3 confirms in a clause, gives the two influence ideas and the task, then ends on "say done" with a single demo offer; turn 4 ends on the read-again question; turns 5 and 6 are short closing lines.
